actions.reason: Strong biological support: RNA shows FDR-significant upregulation of interferon/inflammatory pathways with large effect sizes, and WXS shows significant BAP1 enrichment (q=0.0044). Cross-modal consistency is moderate with median support count 3 and positive RNA/WSI silhouettes. Confounder exclusion shows a significant site enrichment (CJ) but this is a single technical factor and does not override the coherent biological signal. No better-supported structural action or resolvable evidence gap exists.

No significant biological enrichment across RNA, WXS, or CNV; all q-values near 1.0. Strong technical confounding with CT manufacturer/scanner/kernel associations (q<0.05) suggests the set is defined by technical factors rather than biology. Cross-modal consistency shows CT is the only driver (median silhouette 0.276) with weak support from other modalities. The set lacks a defensible biological identity and is better dropped than retained.

No significant biological enrichment across any modality; all q-values high. Cross-modal consistency is weak with near-zero silhouettes in most modalities and only modest WSI support. No significant technical confounders, but the absence of biological signal and lack of structural cohesion indicate the set is not a distinct biological entity. No supported structural action or resolvable evidence gap exists.

Biological support is coherent: RNA shows extensive FDR-significant pathway enrichment (25/50) with large effect sizes, and CNV shows significant lower copy-number on multiple arms (q<0.05). Cross-modal consistency is moderate with positive WSI and RNA silhouettes and high resampling ARI (0.561). No significant technical confounders after correction. The set has a defensible identity with corroborating evidence across modalities.

Biological support is primarily transcriptional with strong RNA pathway enrichment (18/50 FDR-significant, large effect sizes) and coherent directionality. WXS and CNV show only nominal trends, but the RNA signal is robust. Cross-modal consistency shows RNA as the main driver with moderate patient support. No significant technical confounders after correction. The set has a defensible identity based on RNA, and no better-supported structural action or resolvable gap exists.
